title: Maybe, Might & Future Possibilities
description: Discuss uncertain future possibilities without presenting them as facts.
objectives: Discuss uncertain future possibilities without presenting them as facts.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to discuss uncertain future possibilities without presenting them as facts. The central language is might/may plus base verb and maybe. It belongs to the practical context of plans & the future. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: might/may plus base verb and maybe

blocks.english: We might stay an extra day.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the maybe, might & future possibilities exchange.

blocks.english: Maybe I'll take the train instead.
blocks.explanation: This maybe, might & future possibilities model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the maybe, might & future possibilities exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “We might stay an extra day.” and “Maybe I'll take the train instead.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: might/may plus base verb and maybe.
